package_info.package_versions: 1.30.3 (example shown, but technique applies to any version using starjacking)
package_info.why_malicious: The package uses deceptive techniques to artificially inflate its perceived popularity by linking to an unrelated, highly-starred GitHub repository. This misleads users into believing the package is more reputable and widely used than it actually is, undermining trust in open-source ecosystem metrics.

execution_context.file_location: PyPI project metadata (setup.py, pyproject.toml, or direct PyPI web interface)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At package publication, the package metadata is set to reference a popular, unrelated GitHub repository, causing the package manager to display inflated GitHub star and fork counts on the package page, misleading users about the package's popularity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it intentionally links to a repository that is not the actual source code for the published package, with the goal of displaying misleading popularity metrics.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, the homepage or repository URL in package metadata should point to the actual source code or project maintained by the package author. Here, it is used to misrepresent the package's reputation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages link to their own GitHub repository for transparency and collaboration.
key_indicators: Homepage/URL points to a high-star unrelated repository
No code or project relationship between package and linked repo
Inflated star/fork counts on package manager site

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a package to PyPI with metadata linking to a popular, unrelated GitHub repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: PyPI displays misleading GitHub star/fork counts on the package page.

attack_chain.action: Users browsing PyPI see inflated popularity metrics and are misled into believing the package is reputable and widely used.
attack_chain.leads_to: Increased downloads, trust, and potential adoption of a low-quality or malicious package.

behavioral_signatures: Package metadata links to a GitHub repository with no code or author relationship to the package
Sudden appearance of high star/fork counts on new or obscure packages
Discrepancy between package author and GitHub repository owner
file_indicators: setup.py or pyproject.toml with 'url' or 'project_urls' fields pointing to unrelated popular repositories
PyPI project page displaying GitHub stats for unrelated repositories
network_indicators: No direct network indicators (attack is metadata-based), but can monitor for repeated queries to GitHub API for unrelated repositories from package manager infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automate checks for package metadata (setup.py, pyproject.toml, or PyPI web fields) where the homepage or repository URL points to a GitHub repository with no code, commit, or author overlap with the package. Flag packages where the linked repository is significantly more popular than the package's own history or where the repository is unrelated to the package's functionality. Cross-reference package author and GitHub repo owner for mismatches.
